wu: Students play 'PET Bingo' with mixed grammar and vocabulary prompts (e.g., 'Find someone who has visited another country'). They walk around asking questions, mark squares, and shout 'Bingo!' when complete.
wuAlt: Students complete a 'Mid-Year Reflection' worksheet with 5 questions about their progress so far.
Students share one goal they achieved this semester in pairs.
pres: Show the official PET exam map poster on the projector. Explain each section (Reading & Writing, Listening, Speaking) with timing and task types. Use model sentences for strategy language (e.g., 'For Part 1, I need to scan for keywords'). Check understanding with quick thumbs-up/thumbs-down.
presAlt: Distribute PET handbook excerpts and have students highlight key exam details in groups.
Play a 'PET Quiz' with Kahoot! to test their knowledge of the exam format.
prac: Students rotate through 'mini diagnostic stations' (Reading gap-fill, Listening multiple choice, Speaking picture prompt). At each station, they complete 1 PET-style task while the teacher provides feedback on strategies.
pracAlt: Students work in pairs to create their own 3-question PET quiz for their peers.
Complete a 'Strategy Match-Up' activity linking PET tasks to strategies (e.g., 'Part 2 → Read the instructions first').
ls: Students listen to a 5-minute audio tour of the PET exam from the Cambridge website. They fill in a worksheet with section timings and task types, then compare answers in pairs.
re: Play 'PET Relay Race'—teams race to write PET section names on the board after hearing descriptions (e.g., 'This part has 6 questions and a recording').
prod: Students interview a partner about their strengths/weaknesses in English using PET strategy prompts (e.g., 'How do you feel about the speaking test?'). They note 2 goals for each skill.
rw: Students read a short PET-style email (80 words) about a complaint and write a reply using the 'plan, write, check' method. They then swap and mark for content and accuracy.
st: Close with a 'PET Pledge'—students stand and share one spring target. End with: 'Today we mapped the PET exam and set our goals. Thank you for your hard work!'
g: Students rotate every 2 minutes to practice speaking prompts with different partners.
Teams race to write present perfect sentences on the board.
Students toss a ball and name PET-related vocabulary when caught.
Teams race to match headings to PET reading texts.
Students act out PET strategies for others to guess.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a 100-word review of a movie using PET writing Part 1 format.
Support / weaker learners: Use a sentence frame to describe their PET goal (e.g., 'I need to practice ______ to improve my ______.')
hw: Complete 2 PET practice exercises from the workbook (Reading Part 2 & Listening Part 1).
Watch a 3-minute PET speaking video on YouTube and take notes.
Write a 50-word email to a teacher asking for advice on PET preparation.
tip: Emphasize that PET is about real-life communication, not just passing the test. Relate tasks to Moroccan learners' goals (e.g., work, travel, digital skills) to boost motivation.
checklist: I can identify the 4 parts of the PET exam.
I can explain the timing for each section.
I can name 2 strategies for the reading test.
I can set a specific spring target for my speaking.
I can write a 80-word email using PET format.
I can understand a 3-minute PET listening audio.
I can describe my PET preparation plan to a partner.
